title: Late-shift batching hypotheses log — 2026-04-08
content:
Context / why this exists:
- Late-shift note log from the small crew who stayed on to debug a repeatable p50 latency spike seen around 02:00 PT on the canary fleet.
- Primary hypothesis set focuses on batching boundary churn + KV-prefill miss amplification when request sizes vary and kernel scheduling causes micro-starvation.

Attendees / who was noodling:
- Maya Chen (owner for night experiment)
- Ibrahim Ali (oncall), Samira Ortiz (kernel), Felix Nguyen (bench lead)
- Others pinged from SRE async

Observed signal at 02:07-02:22 PT:
- Canary cluster: 3 nodes serving 60% traffic. Sudden p50 jump from 18ms -> 85ms across text-generation routes for ~12 minutes. p90/p99 also increased, but p99 spike was smaller by absolute delta.
- Trace pattern: a subset of requests show extra 40–60ms between enqueue->kernel-run (appears like batching queue pause). KV-cache hit-rate dips by ~6% for sessions with >2 turn conversation.
- Repro steps (local-ish): replay load from staging trace (replay id replay-20260408-02:05) with variable prompt lengths yields 10–15% more queued batches.

Hypotheses (what we think might be happening):
1) Batch boundary thrash: small number of long-running requests (large seq_len) cause the coalescer to hold shorter requests to reach optimal batch sizes — but because the kernel scheduling preempts the worker for a prefetch task, the short requests wait longer than the target window.
2) KV-prefill cold paths: when a request brings a new conversation token pattern, the KV prefill misses trigger an extra kernel phase (prefill then normal run) and that extra phase competes with batching windows causing queue reorder.
3) Kernel affinity jitter: our kernel selection heuristic (ruleset v2) flips kernel variant if measured seq_len changes across micro-batches; switching kernels mid-cohort causes a 30–50ms handoff in some runs.
4) Backpressure feedback loop: coalescer backoff + per-worker sched delay creates a positive feedback that extends the batch wait beyond the SLO for short requests.

Experiments run tonight (config and quick results):
A) Short-window cap: cap coalescer window to 6ms for short-request class (prompt_tokens <= 128). Result: p50 on the sampled route dropped 18% in the synthetic replay, but end-to-end throughput fell ~3% — promising for p50 SLO but cost tradeoff.
B) Disable prefill on canary for tested route: toggled kv-prefill.enabled=false for 2 nodes. Result: KV-hit rate dropped as expected, but p50 latency for short requests improved slightly; long converssions p99 regressed. Suggests that prefill creates additional contention for our observed case.
C) Pin kernel variant: for cohort A, forced kernel-v1 (single variant) instead of auto-switch. Result: transient 35ms reduction on those cohort traces; suggests kernel switch cost is real.

Raw numbers (staging replay):
- baseline p50 18ms, after cap-window test p50 14.6ms (sample window 10k reqs)
- throughput baseline 14.2k tok/s -> 13.8k tok/s (window cap)
- KV-hit rate baseline 86% -> 79% when disabling prefill (expected)

Actionable next steps (prioritized):
1) Short term: roll the short-window cap to full canary for tested route for 24h. Owner: Maya. Reason: best p50 improvement with small throughput hit.
2) Medium term: implement non-blocking prefill paths (SRT-8421) — let prefill execute on spare worker instead of the serving path. Owner: Ibrahim, linked to GH PR #4276.
3) Kernel work: add a cheap check to avoid kernel-variant flips for active cohort windows (<100ms window). Owner: Samira. (Prototype branch kernel/affinity-no-flip)
4) Observability: add a new metric exposing "coalescer_sleep_time_ms" per worker and correlate with kv-prefill-start events. Owner: Felix.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Why did p99 not move as much as p50? Hypothesis: p99 dominated by long seq runs unrelated to coalescer (need to separate traffic).
- Can we have a safe non-prefill fallback that keeps cost+quality balance? (discuss with product).
- Is there a kernel scheduling preemption that is not accounted for in traces (missing trace point)? Need trace instrumentation patch.

Notes-to-self and rough checklist:
- [ ] Patch canary config to add short-window cap at 03:30 PT (post-maint window).
- [ ] Open a small doc for product on prefill tradeoffs (quality vs latency).
- [ ] Add unit test for kernel-variant guard.
- [ ] Schedule 1h sync with SRE on Thursday morning to go through the 02:00 PT time slice in the long retention logs.
- Quick debug commands used: kubectl logs -l canary=true --since=20m; curl -XPOST replay-api/replay?trace=replay-20260408-02:05

Loose ideas / brainstorming (not action yet):
- Could we try a two-tier coalescer: aggressively short-window in known interactive routes and dynamic window for batch jobs?
- Consider a KV-prefill "best-effort" mode that schedules prefill with QoS targeting low-priority worker threads.
- More deterministic kernel handshake: avoid flip if the next batch has >60% same seq_len distribution.

References / tickets mentioned tonight:
- JIRA SRT-8421: non-blocking kv-prefill proposal (created 2026-04-08)
- GH PR: serving-runtime/pull/4276 (bench harness + prefill toggle)
- Replay trace id: replay-20260408-02:05 (staging)

Closing note: overall outcome positive — found multiple plausible contributing mechanisms and a low-risk short-term mitigation that materially improves our p50. Will follow up with a canary roll and reconvene in the morning async thread.

—— end log ——
